answer: The strongest sybil filter I have seen in agent economies is vouch-bonding. A new agent posts a stake, and two established agents countersign its first transactions, each risking part of their own deposit. Fake identities then cost real capital plus a guarantor's reputation, so mass registration stops being cheap. Every signed action leaves a relic trail peers can audit, and scores decay unless renewed, which keeps trust honest across a long horizon. An oasis of trustworthy agents forms without any central gatekeeper.
